The right expectations

What a treatment program can help—and what needs another solution

Good ornamental care begins with identifying the type of problem. Not every yellow leaf, bare branch or declining shrub is caused by an insect, disease or nutrient deficiency.

A strong program fit

Issues We Can Often Help Manage

These are the kinds of recurring pressures a scheduled tree and shrub program is designed to monitor and address.

  • Sucking and chewing insect activity on susceptible plants
  • Mites, scale, lace bugs, aphids and similar ornamental pests
  • Selected foliar disease pressure when treatment is appropriate
  • Plant vigor or color concerns where nutrition is part of the cause
  • Preventive seasonal care for valuable ornamental plantings
May need another specialist

Problems Spraying Cannot Repair

We will not pretend another treatment fixes damage caused by the site, structure or irrigation when it does not.

  • Dead, structurally unsafe or storm-damaged trees
  • Severe root damage, girdling roots or plants installed too deeply
  • Constantly saturated soil, drainage failure or chronic drought
  • Wrong plant for the available sunlight, space or soil
  • Pruning, removal, stump grinding or major arborist work

If the program is not the right answer, we will say so. The goal is to protect the landscape—not sell an application that cannot solve the underlying problem.

Local. Family-owned. Firefighter-owned. Serving Baton Rouge, Ascension, Livingston and nearby communities.
Why Grow Green

A real local team protecting real local landscapes

South Louisiana heat, humidity, rainfall and long growing seasons create their own ornamental challenges. We focus on ornamental treatment work, seasonal timing, and clear communication for South Louisiana trees and shrubs.

  • Common local ornamentals: Care for plants such as azaleas, hollies, camellias, gardenias and other eligible landscape trees and shrubs.
  • Plant-by-plant judgment: Timing and materials can change with the species, condition and pressure present.
  • Clear communication: Know what was treated, what we noticed and any aftercare your landscape needs.
  • No-pressure pricing: Review the proposed program and decide when it makes sense for your property.
Also explore Flower Bed Weed Control →
Good to know

Tree and shrub care questions we hear most

What types of plants can be included?

The program is intended for eligible ornamental trees and shrubs that can be treated safely and effectively on residential properties. Common examples include azaleas, hollies, camellias, gardenias and many other landscape plants. We confirm plant material, size, access and scope during the estimate process.

Why are there six visits instead of one treatment?

Insects, disease pressure, plant growth and nutritional needs change through the year. Six scheduled visits create better timing and repeated observation than waiting until a problem becomes severe and requesting a single rescue treatment.

Is the same product applied during every round?

No. A responsible program can change with the season, plant species, observed pest or disease pressure, weather and product directions. The visit schedule is consistent, but the treatment strategy should respond to what the landscape needs.

Will the program guarantee that my plants never get insects or disease?

No responsible company can guarantee that living plants will never experience pest, disease, weather or site stress. The program is designed to reduce and manage eligible pressure, support plant health and improve the opportunity to catch concerns earlier.

Is service safe around children and pets?

We apply professional products according to their labels. Follow the re-entry instructions provided after each service and keep people and pets away from treated plants until the stated interval has passed.

Do you prune, remove or diagnose hazardous trees?

No. This is a treatment and plant-health program, not pruning, removal or structural tree work. Dead, storm-damaged or potentially hazardous trees should be evaluated by an appropriately qualified tree professional.

Can Tree & Shrub Care be combined with Flower Bed Weed Control?

Yes. They address different needs and can complement each other: Tree & Shrub Care focuses on eligible ornamental plants, while Flower Bed Weed Control focuses on managing weeds in eligible landscape beds.

How is Tree & Shrub Care priced?

Pricing depends on the number, size, type and accessibility of eligible plants, along with the service scope. Send the property address and any concerns through the form so our office can review the landscape and provide straightforward pricing.
